B2.name: FRC.Dirac.Plane.form_class
B2.doc: 8:B2 — the Lorentzian form depends on its coefficient through the class alone: for every `m`, `−(m²ν) x₀² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃² = −ν (m x₀)² + x₁² + x₂² + x₃²`, so the forms of `ν` and `m²ν` are equivalent by the rescaling `x₀ ↦ m x₀` (a polynomial identity, decided by the normaliser).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3 — the drive is a nonsquare on every frame (`m = 1`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.inv_drive_nonsquare
B3.doc: 8:B3, 8:B6 — the reframing flip preserves the class: the inverse of the drive is a nonsquare (an odd power of `g`), so `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.quarter_class
B3.doc: 8:B3 — `i` is a square exactly when the capacity is even (the eighth root of unity exists iff `8 ∣ p − 1`).

B3.name: FRC.Dirac.two_class
B3.doc: 8:B3 — `2`, `2⁻¹` and `−2` are squares exactly when the capacity is even (the second supplementary law at tier 0, 14-entropy's `two_is_square_iff`, and `−1 = (g^κ)²`).

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.nu_factorisation
B4.doc: 8:B4, 8:X2 — the factorisation of the temporal coefficient: `ν = g = 2⁻¹·(2g)` exactly on every shell (`h = 2⁻¹`), and the cofactor `2g` is a square exactly when `κ` is odd — the product `g` odd always (Corollary `coefficient-factors`); the one-way coefficient is the odd step `g`, the two-way constant the Carrier's.

B4.name: FRC.Dirac.carrier_constants
B4.doc: 8:B4 [value] — the laboratory Carrier `Ω = 2 408 561`: the two-way constant `c = 171 106` is a Carrier residue with `c² = 2⁻¹ = 1 204 281`, and the two factors compose, `2⁻¹ · (2g) = 1 204 281 · 12 = 6 = g`.

B5.name: FRC.Dirac.parity_iff
B5.doc: 8:B5, 8:X2 — the square class is chronon parity: on every frame, `g^m` is a square exactly when the drive-step count `m` is even (Theorem `parity`); registered transport `g²` is even, the one-way step `g` odd.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.norm_scale
B6.doc: 8:B6 — norm growth: `N(c z) = c² N(z)` for every base residue `c`; one chronon of drive multiplies every norm by `g²`, a square.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.Ext.mul_conj
B6.doc: 8:B6 — the norm is the product with the conjugate: `z z̄ = N(z)`, a base-field element.

B6.name: FRC.Dirac.inv_drive_nonsquare
B6.doc: 8:B3, 8:B6 — the reframing flip preserves the class: the inverse of the drive is a nonsquare (an odd power of `g`), so `[g⁻¹] = [g]`.

B7.name: FRC.Dirac.zeros13
B7.doc: 8:B7 [value] — on `𝔽₁₃` the Euclidean form has `13³ + 13² − 13 = 2353` zeros and the Lorentzian form (`ν = g = 2`) has `13³ − 13² + 13 = 2041`: the hyperbolic and the elliptic form part on the base shell.

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.herm_star
C2.doc: 8:C2 — the form is Hermitian: `conj ⟨ψ, φ⟩ = ⟨φ, ψ⟩`.

C2.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.herm_nondegenerate
C2.doc: 8:C2 — the form is nondegenerate: a field orthogonal to every field vanishes at every site of the register (its conjugate against the delta field is the site's value).

C4.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.cayley_unitary
C4.doc: 8:C4, 8:D10, 8:X3 — the Cayley step is unitary: for `h` symmetric (`σ h ≈ h`), `a` central with `σ a ≈ −a`, and `v` the inverse of `1 − a h`, the step `u = v (1 + a h)` satisfies `σ(u) u ≈ 1`. The adjoint of `1 − a h` is `1 + a h`, so `σ v` is the inverse of `1 + a h`; `v` commutes with `1 + a h`; and `σ(u) u = (1 − a h) σ(v) v (1 + a h) = (1 − a h) σ(v) (1 + a h) v`.

C4.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.MatE.adjoint_dagger
C4.doc: 8:C4 — the conjugate transpose is an anti-automorphism of the matrix ring: `(AB)† = B†A†`, `(A+B)† = A†+B†`, `1† = 1`, `(−A)† = −A†`, respecting the congruence.

C4.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.cayley_unitary_value
C4.doc: 8:C4 [value] — the Cayley step `U = (1 − wH)⁻¹(1 + wH)` of `H = −Δ` on `𝔽₁₃` (`α = w`, `w̄ = −w`) is unitary, `U†U = 1` (the general statement `cayley_unitary` with `adjoint_dagger`).

C5.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
C5.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:D19, 8:C5, 8:F2, 8:F6 [value] — the norm-one cycle: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `174` on `𝔽₁₇₃` (both `ν = g = 2`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `172` (8:F2).

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley_period
C6.doc: 8:C6, 8:E4 — `DiracML.cayley_period`, its `let`-bound units opened: any proofs `hu`, `hu'` of the two units.

C6.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley13_values
C6.doc: 8:C6, 8:C15, 8:E4, 8:E7, 8:E8 [value] — the Cayley step of `H = −Δ` on `𝔽₁₃` has order exactly `13` at `α = w` and at `α = c = 6w` (`c² = 7 = 2⁻¹`): every Cayley orbit on the shell is periodic, here with the period `13` (C15).

C8.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.herm_translate
C8.doc: 8:C8 — translations are unitary: `⟨T_s ψ, T_s φ⟩ = ⟨ψ, φ⟩`.

C8.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.herm_translate_adjoint
C8.doc: 8:C8 — the adjoint of a translation is the opposite translation: `⟨T_s ψ, φ⟩ = ⟨ψ, T_{p−s} φ⟩` for `s < p`.

C9.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.herm_laplacian
C9.doc: 8:C9 — the Laplacian is self-adjoint, each of its summands being self-adjoint: `T_1` and `T_{p−1}` are adjoint to each other and the diagonal term is real.

C11.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.herm_hamiltonian
C11.doc: 8:C11 — every finite Hamiltonian is self-adjoint: the Laplacian is, the potential is real, and the stiffness is Frobenius-fixed.

C13.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.pullback_translate
C13.doc: 8:C13, 8:D7 — the pullback intertwines the translations: `T_{Ae} (A_* ψ) = A_* (T_e ψ)` at every point.

C13.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.pullback_fwdDiff
C13.doc: 8:C13, 8:D7 — the pullback intertwines the forward differences: `∂_{Ae} (A_* ψ) = A_* (∂_e ψ)` at every point, so the transported difference operator is the difference along the transported direction.

C13.name: FRC.Dirac.Hermitian.pullback_symDiff

C15.name: FRC.Dirac.cayley13_values

C16.name: FRC.Dirac.Plane.cayley_gauge
C16.doc: 8:C16 — the orientation gauge inverts every value of the Cayley map: `φ⁻(λ) φ(λ) = 1` when `(1 − νλ²) u = 1` (the product is `(N u)²` on the real line and `0` on the imaginary one, two polynomial identities).

D3.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.dirac_factorisation

D3.doc: 8:D3 [value] — the factorisation in `0+1` on `𝔽₁₃` (`ν = 2`, `i = 5`), on the kernels of the translation-invariant operators: for `𝒟^s = ∇^s ⊗ γ⁰` and `m = 1`, `(𝒟^s − m)(𝒟^s + m) = −ν (∇^s)² ⊗ I₄ − m²`, as `dirac_factorisation` states with `η₀ = γ⁰γ⁰ = −ν`.

D9.name: FRC.Dirac.spinor_form_values
D9.doc: 8:D9, 8:X4 [value] — the spinor form on `𝔽₁₃`, `𝔽₁₇₃` and `𝔽₁₅₄₉`: the `γ⁰`-twist fails and `X = γ⁰γ¹γ³` is the form the arithmetic forces.

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.cayley_nilpotent_shift
D10.doc: 8:D10 — the Cayley step of a nilpotent shift minus a mass. With `α`, `m` central, `a = 1 + α m` a central unit of inverse `a'`, `b = 1 − α m`, and `N` nilpotent (`N^{k+1} ≈ 0`): `1 − α(N − m) = a (1 − a' α N)` is a unit, with inverse `V = geom (a' α N) (k+1) · a'`, and the step `U = V (1 + α(N − m))` differs from the scalar phase `b a'` by `N c` with `c` commuting with `N`. The massless step (`m = 0`, `b = a = a' = 1`) is `1 + N c`.

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.nilpotent_of_eq_mul
D10.doc: 8:D10 — the step minus the phase is nilpotent: `(U − b a')^{k+1} ≈ 0` when `U − b a' ≈ N c`, `N c ≈ c N`, `N^{k+1} ≈ 0`. With the phase central, `U^{(k+1)} ≈ (b a')^{k+1}` follows in characteristic `p` for `k + 1 = p` (the unipotent file); the massless step has `b a' = 1`.

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.opow_of_nilpotent_shift
D10.doc: 8:D10 — a unipotent step has order dividing `p`: `(u − 1)^p ≈ 0` gives `u^p ≈ 1`, and a phase times a unipotent, `u ≈ φ + N` with `φ` central and `N^p ≈ 0`, `N` commuting with `φ`, has `u^p ≈ φ^p`.

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.MatE.adjoint_twist
D10.doc: 8:C4, 8:D10 — the `X`-adjoint `A ↦ X' A† X` of a unit `X` (`X X' ≈ 1`) is an adjoint too: the spinor form's adjoint is an anti-automorphism, so the Cayley step of an `X`-self-adjoint operator preserves the `X`-form (`cayley_unitary` with this adjoint).

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.MatE.symdiff_nilpotent
D10.doc: 8:D10, 8:X3 — the symmetric difference `∇^s = h (T − T⁻¹)` is nilpotent on every frame, `(∇^s)^p ≈ 0`: `(T − T⁻¹)^p ≈ T^p + (−T⁻¹)^p ≈ 1 − 1` by the Frobenius, `T⁻¹ = T^{p−1}`, and the central `h` factors out.

D10.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.translation_values13

D14.name: FRC.Dirac.Plane.boost_orthogonal

D15.name: FRC.Dirac.Plane.boost_of_mul

D15.name: FRC.Shell.Frame.boost_comp_t

E2.doc: 8:E2 — a self-map of `[0, n)` is bijective exactly when its image count is `n` (the loss factor, the count over the image count, is one): surjectivity is the count of the hit values, and injectivity follows from surjectivity by the pigeonhole — with a collision `f i = f j`, `i ≠ j`, the `n − 1` values of `f` off `j` would still cover `[0, n)`.

E8.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
E8.doc: 8:F4, 8:F6, 8:X1, 8:E8 — sector separation: the inverse of the drive is primitive of order `p − 1` (`ord(g⁻¹) = p − 1`, so the free evolution is no Cayley step, whose scalar phases have order dividing `p + 1`), and the norm-one cycle meets the base field in `{±1}` alone (`u² = 1 ⇒ u = ±1`): the two spectra meet in the two signs.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.ladder
F2.doc: 8:F2 — the ladder `1, …, 2κ`: `κ + 1`, the first rung past the midpoint `κ`, is still a rung.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.four_kappa
F2.doc: 8:F2 — `4κ ≡ −1` on the shell (`4κ = p − 1`), so `κ = −4⁻¹` and the energy radius `1 + κ = 3·4⁻¹`.

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.terminal_latitude
F2.doc: 8:F2 — the terminal latitude: `π = 2κ = −2⁻¹`; the quarter-cycle shift `m ↦ m + κ` on the ladder is multiplication by `g^κ = −i` (`quarterTurn_eq_pow`, `i = −g^κ` by definition).

F2.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
F2.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:D19, 8:C5, 8:F2, 8:F6 [value] — the norm-one cycle: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `174` on `𝔽₁₇₃` (both `ν = g = 2`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `172` (8:F2).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3, 8:F6 — the drive pullback on the characters: with `y = g⁻¹`, `χ_k(g^{j}) = y^k · χ_k(g^{j+1})` for every `j, k` — the winding-`k` mode acquires the phase `g^{−k}` per chronon, so the drive is semisimple with the whole drive cycle as its spectrum (Theorem `zonal` (2), Proposition `two-spectra`).

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.exceptional_eigen
F3.doc: 8:F3 — the exceptional eigenvalue: `k = 2κ` gives `g^{−2κ} = −1` (and `k = 0` gives `1`) — the intersection `N¹ ∩ μ_{p−1} = {±1}` of the norm-one torus with the phase cycle.

F3.name: FRC.Dirac.isotropy
F3.doc: 8:F3 — isotropy: the character line `χ_k` is isotropic, `Σ_j χ_k(g^j)² = Σ_j g^{2jk} = 0`, unless `(p − 1) ∣ 2k`; on the two exceptional lines the sum is `p − 1 = −1 ≠ 0` (Theorem `zonal` (3)).

F4.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
F4.doc: 8:F4, 8:F6, 8:X1, 8:E8 — sector separation: the inverse of the drive is primitive of order `p − 1` (`ord(g⁻¹) = p − 1`, so the free evolution is no Cayley step, whose scalar phases have order dividing `p + 1`), and the norm-one cycle meets the base field in `{±1}` alone (`u² = 1 ⇒ u = ±1`): the two spectra meet in the two signs.

F6.name: FRC.Dirac.drive_eigen
F6.doc: 8:F3, 8:F6 — the drive pullback on the characters: with `y = g⁻¹`, `χ_k(g^{j}) = y^k · χ_k(g^{j+1})` for every `j, k` — the winding-`k` mode acquires the phase `g^{−k}` per chronon, so the drive is semisimple with the whole drive cycle as its spectrum (Theorem `zonal` (2), Proposition `two-spectra`).

F6.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
F6.doc: 8:F4, 8:F6, 8:X1, 8:E8 — sector separation: the inverse of the drive is primitive of order `p − 1` (`ord(g⁻¹) = p − 1`, so the free evolution is no Cayley step, whose scalar phases have order dividing `p + 1`), and the norm-one cycle meets the base field in `{±1}` alone (`u² = 1 ⇒ u = ±1`): the two spectra meet in the two signs.

F6.name: FRC.Dirac.torus_counts
F6.doc: 8:D5, 8:D12, 8:D19, 8:C5, 8:F2, 8:F6 [value] — the norm-one cycle: `|N¹| = 14 = p + 1` on `𝔽₁₃` and `174` on `𝔽₁₇₃` (both `ν = g = 2`); the unit-norm circle of the chart has `p − 1` points: `12` and `172` (8:F2).

F7.name: FRC.Dirac.Plane.dispersion
F7.doc: 8:F7 — the dispersion relation: on the drive cycle, `χ_k(j) = g^{jk}` and the cycle Laplacian `(Δχ)(j) = χ(j+1) + χ(j−1) − 2χ(j)` acts on `χ_k` as the scalar `g^k + g^{−k} − 2`: at the site `j + 1`, `χ_k(j+2) = g^k χ_k(j+1)` and `χ_k(j) = y^k χ_k(j+1)` with `y = g⁻¹` (`drive_eigen`).

F7.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.translation_nilpotent
F7.doc: 8:F7, 8:D10 — the translations are unipotent: on the frame's shell (`p = 4κ + 1`), in characteristic `p`, `t^p ≈ 1` gives `(t − 1)^p ≈ t^p + (−1)^p ≈ 1 − 1 ≈ 0` (`t` and `−1` commute; the Frobenius is additive).

F7.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.MatE.translation_unipotent
F7.doc: 8:F7 — the translations are unipotent on every frame: `(T − 1)^p ≈ 0` on the cycle of `p` sites, by `translation_nilpotent` with `T^p ≈ 1` and the characteristic.

F7.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.static_unique
F7.doc: 8:X3, 8:F7 — the static massive equation `(N − m) ψ ≈ 0` has only the zero solution, `N − m` being a unit.

F7.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.translation_values13
F7.doc: 8:F7, 8:D10, 8:X3 [value] — on the cycle of `𝔽₁₃`: the translation has `T^p = 1`, `T − 1` is nilpotent, `(T − 1)^p = 0`, and the symmetric difference `∇^s = 2⁻¹(T − T⁻¹)` is nilpotent, `(∇^s)^p = 0` (the kinetic sector unipotent; the general statements `translation_nilpotent` and `series_inverse`).

X1.name: FRC.Dirac.sector_separation
X1.doc: 8:F4, 8:F6, 8:X1, 8:E8 — sector separation: the inverse of the drive is primitive of order `p − 1` (`ord(g⁻¹) = p − 1`, so the free evolution is no Cayley step, whose scalar phases have order dividing `p + 1`), and the norm-one cycle meets the base field in `{±1}` alone (`u² = 1 ⇒ u = ±1`): the two spectra meet in the two signs.

X2.name: FRC.Dirac.nu_factorisation
X2.doc: 8:B4, 8:X2 — the factorisation of the temporal coefficient: `ν = g = 2⁻¹·(2g)` exactly on every shell (`h = 2⁻¹`), and the cofactor `2g` is a square exactly when `κ` is odd — the product `g` odd always (Corollary `coefficient-factors`); the one-way coefficient is the odd step `g`, the two-way constant the Carrier's.

X2.name: FRC.Dirac.parity_iff
X2.doc: 8:B5, 8:X2 — the square class is chronon parity: on every frame, `g^m` is a square exactly when the drive-step count `m` is even (Theorem `parity`); registered transport `g²` is even, the one-way step `g` odd.

X3.name: FRC.Dirac.Spinor.MatE.symdiff_nilpotent
X3.doc: 8:D10, 8:X3 — the symmetric difference `∇^s = h (T − T⁻¹)` is nilpotent on every frame, `(∇^s)^p ≈ 0`: `(T − T⁻¹)^p ≈ T^p + (−T⁻¹)^p ≈ 1 − 1` by the Frobenius, `T⁻¹ = T^{p−1}`, and the central `h` factors out.

X3.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.static_unique
X3.doc: 8:X3, 8:F7 — the static massive equation `(N − m) ψ ≈ 0` has only the zero solution, `N − m` being a unit.

X3.name: FRC.Dirac.Operator.cayley_unitary
X3.doc: 8:C4, 8:D10, 8:X3 — the Cayley step is unitary: for `h` symmetric (`σ h ≈ h`), `a` central with `σ a ≈ −a`, and `v` the inverse of `1 − a h`, the step `u = v (1 + a h)` satisfies `σ(u) u ≈ 1`. The adjoint of `1 − a h` is `1 + a h`, so `σ v` is the inverse of `1 + a h`; `v` commutes with `1 + a h`; and `σ(u) u = (1 − a h) σ(v) v (1 + a h) = (1 − a h) σ(v) (1 + a h) v`.

X4.name: FRC.Dirac.spinor_form_values
X4.doc: 8:D9, 8:X4 [value] — the spinor form on `𝔽₁₃`, `𝔽₁₇₃` and `𝔽₁₅₄₉`: the `γ⁰`-twist fails and `X = γ⁰γ¹γ³` is the form the arithmetic forces.
